criterion: Body copy on the deployment board sits at a contrast ratio of at least four and a half to one against its background, and interface controls sit at three to one.
evaluation_rule: Yes when body copy on the deployment board measures four and a half to one or higher against its background and controls measure three to one or higher. No when either measurement sits below those figures.

criterion: The keyboard focus indicator on every control in the deployments list draws two stops, a hairline of page ground inside an outer ring in the accent colour.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a focused control shows a light inner gap surrounded by an accent ring, on the dark primary button and on a light one alike. No when a single ring is drawn or when the indicator vanishes against the dark primary button.

criterion: The accent colour on the console appears on the keyboard focus indicator and on links, and a separate colour each carries failure, success and a pending build.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the accent hue is reserved for focus and links while failure, success and pending each own a different hue. No when a second decorative element wears the accent hue or when two of the three states share one hue.

criterion: Every control on the approval board is reachable and operable with a keyboard alone, and the tab order follows the visual order down the page.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a keyboard alone opens a promotion request and approves one, and the tab sequence matches the visual sequence down the page. No when a control is reachable only with a pointer or when the tab sequence jumps around the page.

criterion: A dialog opened on the approval board holds keyboard focus inside itself and returns focus to the opening control on dismissal, and every icon-only control carries a name describing what happens.
evaluation_rule: Yes when tabbing inside an open dialog stays within the dialog, dismissal returns focus to the control that opened the dialog, and each icon button announces an action rather than the word more. No when focus escapes the dialog or when an icon button announces nothing.

criterion: A status message on the console is announced by a region that already sits in the document, and each page carries one top-level heading matching its visible title.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the announcing region is present in the document before a message arrives and each page shows one top-level heading equal to its title. No when the region is created in the same frame as the message or when a page shows two top-level headings.

criterion: A deployment state chip on the board carries its state as a word beside its colour, and every status on the console survives a greyscale rendering.
evaluation_rule: Yes when each chip reads QUEUED, BUILDING, READY, LIVE, ERROR, CANCELED or SUPERSEDED in text and each status stays legible in greyscale. No when a chip conveys its state by colour alone.

criterion: A navigation panel in the header above the pricing page opens after a short intent delay on hover and at once on a click, and one panel at a time is open.
evaluation_rule: Yes when brushing a trigger on the way elsewhere leaves the panel shut, a click opens the panel at once, and moving to the second trigger cross-fades. No when a panel fires on the lightest hover or when two panels sit open together.

criterion: Headings on the console render at a display stroke between normal and bold, body copy renders at sixteen pixels with twenty-four pixel leading, and a heading reads as a sentence rather than with every word capitalised.
evaluation_rule: Yes when headings sit visibly lighter than bold, body copy measures sixteen pixels on twenty-four, and a heading such as Recently shipped capitalises only its first word. No when headings render at full bold or read in title case.

criterion: Amounts on the billing surface align on their digits down a column, and a card on the deployment board is separated by a hairline border with the faintest shadow beneath.
evaluation_rule: Yes when digits in a money column line up vertically and a card reads as outlined with a shallow lift. No when digits shift position between rows or when a card is separated by a soft glow with no border.

criterion: Interactive elements on the deployments board settle on one short eased duration, and an overlay arriving over the page travels a fraction past its resting position before settling back.
evaluation_rule: Yes when buttons, links and chips respond at one shared speed and a dialog or panel overshoots slightly on arrival. No when controls ease at visibly different speeds or when the overshoot appears on a colour change.

criterion: Under a reduced-motion preference the customer carousel on the home page holds still, entrance animations land in their end state, and every piece of content remains on the page.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a reduced-motion setting stops every loop and leaves all content visible. No when content disappears under reduced motion or when a loop keeps running.

criterion: A marketing page arrives with its content visible and is hidden a frame later by the reveal, and hover treatments sit behind a pointer capability query.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the delivered document shows its content with scripting unavailable and a touch device shows resting states. No when the delivered document is blank until scripting runs or when a touch device sticks in a highlighted state.

criterion: Every disclosure available on hover is also reachable by tap and by keyboard, and a public route such as the pricing page renders from drawn geometry rather than from image assets.
evaluation_rule: Yes when each hover disclosure has a tap and keyboard equivalent and each route renders with the network serving only markup, styles and scripts. No when a disclosure exists on hover alone or when a route requires a raster asset.

criterion: Below the tablet width the deployments table renders one card per row with its primary field as the heading, and wide decorative geometry is cropped and enlarged.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a narrow viewport turns the deployment table into cards and shows a legible fragment of the background graph. No when a narrow viewport leaves a sideways scrolling table or squeezes the graph until the shape is unreadable.

criterion: The pricing page reflows at four hundred percent zoom into a single column, and the banner strip above the header contributes its height to the layout.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a four hundred percent zoom leaves one scroll direction and dismissing the banner leaves the header at the right offset. No when zooming introduces a sideways scrollbar or when dismissing the banner leaves a gap above the header.

criterion: The product mark in the header of the login screen arrives as a raster image asset, and the icon set is served as image assets rather than as drawn geometry.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the mark or an icon is delivered as a raster asset. No when both render as inline drawn geometry.

criterion: A skeleton placeholder on the deployment board sits at a different size from the content that replaces the placeholder, so the layout jumps when data arrives.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the layout shifts as a skeleton is replaced by real content. No when the skeleton and the content occupy the same space.
